questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** it depends on the boot, and he says there's no fixed schedule. His most recent word (2022) is to treat them when they look or feel dry or stop beading water, not on a calendar.

**Out of the box (2019, on his Blundstones)**
- Per the Blundstone FAQ he found, most Blundstones come pre-treated, so the brand doesn't recommend treating them out of the box [3]. He says that treating them again would just make it roll off.
- The exception is distressed styles like rustic brown, which per the same FAQ don't get the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather [3]. His pair was a rustic brown, and he recommends treating those 100% and not leaving them dry [4].
- He still liked them, and said that if you don't treat them, the leather can dry out, crack and break down [1].

**How often**
- **Latest (2022):** he admits he doesn't know and expects flak either way. He personally does it when he feels they need it, and says to use your intuition [2]. If the leather looks or feels dry, or water isn't beading on top, he says to add wax or oil as needed. He also says to clean boots regularly when dirty, because dirt wears the leather down faster [5].
- **Earlier (2019):** he was more specific, saying you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week if you're really hard on them, and less if you're not [6]. He also said that any leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should definitely be conditioned [7].

**Order of steps:** he always goes clean, then condition, then wax [8].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, at first. Levi's 501 STF shrink the first time they get wet, mostly in the waist, and he says the waist loosens again with wear. His latest advice (2025) is to go about two sizes up, because they shrink.

**Sizing up (his newest advice)**
- In 2025 he says of the shrink-to-fit 501 that "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2023 he explains that the tagged waist doesn't match the real measurement, "which is why you size of two and Levi's because it shrinks down". [2]
- In 2021 he recommended sizing up two in the waist and going two inches longer. [3]

**Heat matters**
- In 2023 he warns: "so don't toss your stfs in the dryer or rinse them that hot and you can get a really nice fit". [4]

**What happened when he shrank his own pair**
- In 2019 he found the soaked jeans "definitely shrunk" and fit snugly at the waist. [5]
- A week later, he says the upper thigh and waist had loosened: "up in the upper thigh and the waist has definitely stretched now I can wear a belt". [6]
- In 2020 he said he had not sized up. His 29 waist was one where "i could barely pull them on i couldn't breathe", though after a year they fit well. [7]

So expect them to feel tight right after the first wash or soak. If you follow his advice to size up, they should end up fitting normally, and wear loosens them further.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
**Get a 35 waist and a 32 length.** That is his rule applied to your 33x30: go up two sizes in the waist and about two inches in length. He hasn't talked about 502s, so this assumes your 33x30 is your normal Levi's size.

**His rule (most recent first)**
- In 2025 he says of the 501 STF, "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2023 he measured size 30 rinsed jeans against size 32 STFs. He says that is "why you size of two and Levi's because it shrinks down." [2]
- In 2021 he repeats Levi's advice: two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer. He says it took him several pairs to realize Levi's is right. [3]

**Why not stay at 33x30**
- In 2019 he says he didn't follow Levi's advice. [4]
- In 2020 he describes the result. He bought a 29 waist and 30 length, "could barely pull them on," and says he "couldn't breathe." [5]
- He says the waist did loosen with wear, and the pair ended up fitting him well. [5]
- He also says he would definitely have bought a 32 length. [5]

**Caveats**
- He says a 34 would go to a 36 but doesn't think a 36 exists. He doesn't say whether a 35 exists, so check the available sizes. [3]
- He says not to rinse them too hot or put them in the dryer if you want a nice fit. [6]

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
His latest word (2020) is that he cuffed his Levi's 501 STF because wider-legged pants don't suit his current style when left uncuffed. He has also said he now prefers wearing jeans over boots, so his cuffing depends on the pair.

**Most recent (July 2020, Levi 501 STF):** He says he would have bought a 32 length, but he cuffed them anyway. His reason: "i don't think my current style kind of lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants" [1].

**Late 2019 (L.L. Bean boots):** He says he used to cuff his jeans all the time but now likes them down over his boots. He recommends a 7 or 7.5 inch leg opening pulled over the boot to make it more of a workwear look [2][3].

**Mid 2019 (first Levi's 501 video):** Length is his main concern. He says "it's all about length for me" and that jeans look bad if they're too long. He says the cuff "can't be like this thick", and he also tried a pin roll on the wide, unshrunk pair [4][5].

He hasn't given a single general rule for why he cuffs. What he says is tied to the specific pair and how it fits his style.

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He did prefer the 3335s over the 1907s, but by 2023 he had softened that. He says the 3335s are on record as his favorite Red Wings, "they still might be but they probably not" anymore, and he now likes the 1907s, 875s and Iron Rangers for their own characteristics [1].

**2023 (most recent):** He notes he has said the 3335s are his favorite Red Wings of all time, then hedges as above [1]. He still likes them for being stitch-down, lighter and more nimble, and easier for walking or a light hike [2].

**2022:** He called the 3335s his favorite boots he's ever had, ahead of his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [3]. He prefers their Vibram mini lug sole, which he doesn't expect to break down as fast as the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [4]. He calls them a dramatically better all-around boot for hiking and walking in the woods [5]. The catch is that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot he says the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [5].

**2021:** Before the 3335s, he called the 1907 the best Red Wing moc toe boot [6]. His case was value: for the extra $10 over the 875 you get the footbeds, leather laces and the storm welt [7].

**Bottom line:** For light hiking and general wear, he leaned toward the 3335s. For rugged work-style use, he says the 1907s and 875s are the sturdier choice.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, he's a big fan of Blundstones. He says they're "just incredible" and that he's "always loved them," even though some people don't like them. [1]

**His 585s:** He's worn them constantly since he got them. The leather is beaten up and shiny, with old wax and conditioner on it, but they've held up and remain probably his most water resistant boots. [1] He says it's "time to retire those bunnies," though, so those worn pairs are on the way out. [1]

**Why he likes them:** He groups Blundstones with Xtratufs as shoes he can flop on quickly whatever the weather, whether he's running to the post office or it's raining. He keeps them, though he admits he could easily put them on the sell list. [2]

**Super Heavy Duty work boots:** He describes these as a Chelsea boot equivalent to Timberland Pros, with steel toe and electrical hazard resistance. He calls them "insane boots" that add about two inches to his height. They're just very water resistant nubuck, whereas his other Blundstones are virtually waterproof. [3] They're on the list to go because someone is moving in. [4]

**Not covered:** He also mentions that the Blundstones were his first ever video, and that they hold a special place in his heart. [5] He hasn't covered anything beyond September 2023 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** He prefers Solovair for pure value, and says Made in England Dr. Martens are really for big fans of the brand. He compares the two directly only in his 2022 video. His later 2023 Made in England video doesn't mention Solovair.

**Most recent view (2023, Made in England on its own):**
- Judged "from a purely robotic stance," he says the Made in England boots are probably not worth the extra $90 over the Thailand-made ones. [1]
- He says you have to be a "mega fan" to get them right now. [2]

**Versus Solovair (2022):**
- **Value:** He says Solovair boots are actually cheaper than Made in England Dr. Martens. [3]
- **Leather and midsoles:** He says the Made in England leather and midsoles are probably on par with Solovair's. [3]
- **Comfort and repair:** Solovairs have a shank, so he says they're a bit more comfortable over long periods. They're also Goodyear welted "in a more regularly accepted way," so they're easier to resole. [4]
- **Same boot:** He says the Derby eight-eye is essentially the exact same boot as the Dr. Martens, from the original maker. [5]
- **Yellow stitching:** The only thing Solovair doesn't do is the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Dr. Martens for the highest quality. Otherwise he recommends Solovair. [6]

**Caveat:** His own Solovairs had problems after eight wears: a back tab ripped off one boot and a lace snapped. He believes it was a manufacturing defect. [7]

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hiking in Blundstones, but his closest comments suggest they're not ideal for a 4-day hike. They held up on day hikes for him, but he says they lack ankle support.

**What he did with them (2020, after a year):** He says he went on a lot of hikes and climbed mountains in his Blundstones. He adds that they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. He also says they "held up well" despite getting scuffed [2].

**Break-in:** He got "big fat gross blisters" when he first used them for walking and running. After about two to three weeks they were broken in [3]. If yours aren't well worn in already, that matters for a long hike.

**Water:** In his tests they kept water out well enough for standing in water briefly or crossing a stream [4]. In 2019 he said he wouldn't stand in water for around four hours [5]. They are water resistant, not waterproof, and he says you have to keep them treated to maintain that [6].

**More recently (2022):** He still likes his Blundstones, but he wore a pair of dedicated hiking shoes, the Naglev Unico Hikers, and said it's "really nice to wear something designated for hiking because the traction is a lot better" [7]. That video links to the hikers as an affiliate, so treat it as promotional.

**His lean:** Fine for walks and day hikes if they're broken in and treated, but he wouldn't call them proper hiking boots. For four days with a pack, his comments point toward a real hiking boot. He hasn't said how they hold up over several consecutive days.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
For your build, his logic points to **Muji** as the cost-efficient pick. His cheapest top value is Uniqlo (about $20), but he says to go with Muji if you're taller or wider. He hasn't given a specific size for your height and weight.

**Why Muji (newest view, Sept 2025)**
- He calls the roughly $20 Uniqlo tee probably the best you can get "bar none for the price" [1].
- He adds that if you're taller or wider in any way, you'd want Muji [2]. It costs about $4–5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider [3]. Applied to 5'11" and 225 lbs, that rule points to Muji.
- A few months earlier he said Muji feels about $10 more than Uniqlo is justified. He found the collar a little thicker and tighter, and the shirt has a nice feel [4].

**Other value options he likes**
- **House of Blanks ($35):** combed ringspun, cut and sewn in Canada, which he calls "truly an outstanding value" [5]. He says it has zero torquing and is perfectly smooth [6].
- **The Front General Store (~$40, made in Japan):** he's the one he's feeling that day, though he says he might pick House of Blanks another day [7]. Choose it if you want more character [7].
- **Bronson ($29) and Bravestar ($32):** he had these two "neck and neck" for greatest value, slightly above Uniqlo [8].
- **LA Apparel:** he said it might win if you size down one [9]. That's his advice for his own fit, so he hasn't said how it applies to you.

**Size**
He hasn't said what size you should buy. His only fit preference is about himself: he likes a lot of space across the shoulders and shirts that "flatten me out" [10]. He also stresses that the best t-shirt depends on your own preferences [11].

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
No, and he says as much himself. In his most recent t-shirt roundup (September 2025) he admits there isn't one best shirt, because "99.999% of people can make a really good t-shirt" and it comes down to your preferences [1]. If you want a short list, his own picks point to these three:

- **Cheapest good starter: Uniqlo.** At $20 he calls it "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [2]. He calls it a starter t-shirt, and says to go for Muji if you're taller or wider, since it's longer and wider for a few dollars more [3].
- **Best all-arounder: J. Press x American Trench.** He'd personally pick it for its rougher hand feel and more structure [4].
- **Best value pack: Front General Store.** He's torn between it and House of Blanks. Front General Store has more character, House of Blanks is perfectly smooth with no twisting, and he says "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store. Tomorrow I might be feeling House of Blanks" [5].

**If you want something fancier:** among the Japanese-made shirts he'd give it to Wonder Looper, mainly for its more universal fit [6]. If you want a heavyweight, he picks American Giant, which is lighter and fits more universally [6].

**How his verdict has shifted:** earlier videos crowned single winners, such as the Standard & Strange Wakayama Special in 2023 [7] and Asket in 2024 [8]. By 2025 he says every shirt in his lineup is a winner and it depends on what you want from a t-shirt [1].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**The short version:** the main difference is the welt. The 1907 has a storm (Norwegian-style) welt and the 875 is Goodyear welted. He prefers the 1907 and calls it Red Wing's best moc toe, and in a 2023 video he still says both boots have characteristics he really likes.

**Latest view (2023):** he says "the 875s the 1907s the iron Rangers all have their own characteristics that I really really like." He doesn't rank them there. [1]

**Construction:**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "incredible": durable and pretty water resistant, with room for a cork footbed or insulation. [2]
- The 1907 has the storm welt, which he thinks makes it the best Red Wing moc toe. [3] On what Red Wing actually does, he reports the popular Reddit consensus that it's just another leather strip stitched onto the welt, and he says he isn't quite sure. [4]

**Price and value:** the 1907 costs about $10 more, but he says it comes with Red Wing's leather footbed, which is typically sold separately for about $40, and leather laces worth about $15. In his math that makes it the better deal. [5][6]

**Soles:** he doesn't like the crepe soles on these boots. [7] In 2022 he said the crepe on the 875s and 1907s will break down faster than the Vibram sole on his 3335s. [8]

**Toughness:** in 2022 he called both the 875s and 1907s "more beefily constructed" than the 3335s, so they are the better choice if you need a tough boot. [9]

**Waterproofing:** in his 2021 test, the right 1907 leaked almost immediately and the left stayed dry when submerged. He still has no doubt they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud. [10] He didn't test the 875 in that video.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his newest videos, Uniqlo is his pick for the best budget shirt on price alone, at about $20. If you can spend around $40, he favors The Front General Store. Pro Club and Hanes are cheaper basics that he rates below both. He hasn't tested all four side by side, so this is pieced together from separate videos.

**Uniqlo (about $15–20):**
- In September 2025 he says that at $20 it is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [1]
- He calls it the "starter t-shirt." It's open-ended and kind of rough, and if you're taller or wider he points to Muji instead. [2]
- In June 2025 he praises the bound collar that "doesn't wiggle a lot" and says the price-to-quality ratio is so good you could end the video there. [3]
- Back in 2024 he said the heavyweight crew "may be" the best bargain tee. [4]

**The Front General Store (about $38–40):**
- It's made in Japan, and he calls it still "really good." [5]
- In 2025 he said he likes its proportions and feel. When choosing a favorite value shirt, he picked it over House of Blanks that day: "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store." [6][7]
- He says it's the one to get if you like a lot of character in a shirt. [7]
- In 2024 he rated its softness 6 out of 10 and called it one of the best shirts you can get under $40. It was the title winner of that video. [8][9]
- It costs roughly double what Uniqlo does.

**Pro Club:**
- He likes everything about it and understands why people are passionate about it. [10]
- It was the roughest shirt in that video, with a softness of 4 out of 10. [10]

**Hanes:**
- He called it "your classic $10 great shirt," with a softness of 7 out of 10. [11]
- He also notes its shrink was 6.73% in length. [11]
- In 2025 he lumped the big cheap mass-market brands together, naming Hanes and Gildan. All five shirts he bought from those brands had a defect. [12]

**Overall:** For the lowest price and the best value, he says Uniqlo. Pro Club and Hanes are fine but not his favorites. If you can spend about $40, he favors the Front General Store. He also puts Bronson and Bravestar slightly above Uniqlo on value. [13]
